Feedback Widget is a floating feedback button for React that morphs open from the screen corner into a small popup, built with Framer Motion and Tailwind CSS. Users type a message and submit it, the button shows a sending state, a check draws on success and the popup closes on its own, while a failed send keeps the message and offers a retry. It sits in the bottom right or bottom left corner.When to use itA beta product wants a lightweight way to collect bug reports and ideas from any page.A documentation site asks readers for feedback without sending them to a separate form.An internal tool needs a quick channel for staff to report problems.AccessibilityThe corner trigger is a button named by the title prop with aria-haspopup set to dialog, and the message field is labelled by the popup title. The field takes focus once the popup has opened, Escape or a click outside closes it except while a message is sending, and a failed send is shown in an element with the alert role. With reduced motion enabled, the panel content fades in and out without sliding, scaling or blurring, and the field is focused right away.FAQHow do I add a feedback button to a React app?Install the block and render FeedbackWidget near the root of your layout with an onSubmit handler. onSubmit receives an object with the message.How do I send the feedback to my backend?Make onSubmit async and post the message inside it. The widget shows Sending until the promise resolves, shows success when it does, and switches to a retry state if it throws.Can I move it to the left corner or change the text?Yes. Set position to "bottom-left", and use title, placeholder and icon to change the heading, the field hint and the trigger icon.
